subject: math.RA
name: Artin-Wedderburn theorem
statement: A semisimple Artinian ring is isomorphic to a finite product of full matrix rings over division rings. Conversely, every such finite product is semisimple Artinian.

subject: math.RA
name: Wedderburn little theorem
statement: Every finite division ring is commutative and hence is a finite field.

subject: math.RA
name: Jacobson density theorem
statement: Let M be a simple left module over a ring R and put D=End_R(M) opposite, so M is a right D-vector space. For any finite D-linearly independent vectors v_1, ..., v_n and any vectors w_1, ..., w_n, some r in R satisfies rv_i=w_i for every i.

subject: math.RA
name: Hopkins-Levitzki theorem
statement: Every left Artinian ring is left Noetherian. The analogous statement holds on the right.

subject: math.RA
name: Wedderburn-Malcev theorem
statement: Let A be a finite-dimensional associative algebra over a perfect field and J its Jacobson radical. There is a semisimple subalgebra S such that A is the direct sum of S and J as vector spaces and S maps isomorphically onto A/J.

subject: math.RA
name: Skolem-Noether theorem
statement: Every automorphism of a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field k that fixes k pointwise is inner: it has the form x maps to uxu^(-1) for an invertible element u of the algebra.

subject: math.RA
name: Double centralizer theorem for central simple algebras
statement: If A is a finite-dimensional central simple k-algebra and B is a central simple k-subalgebra with the same identity, then its centralizer C_A(B) is central simple over k and multiplication gives an isomorphism B tensor_k C_A(B) to A.

references.title: Double centralizer theorem for central simple algebras

subject: math.RA
name: Amitsur-Levitzki theorem
statement: For every commutative ring R, the matrix ring M_n(R) satisfies the standard polynomial identity of degree 2n: the alternating sum over all permutations of products of 2n matrices is zero.

subject: math.RA
name: Kaplansky theorem on primitive PI rings
statement: A primitive ring satisfying a polynomial identity is a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over its center. In particular, it is a matrix ring over a division ring of finite dimension over its center.

references.title: Kaplansky theorem on primitive PI rings

subject: math.RA
name: Goldie theorem
statement: A semiprime ring satisfying the ascending chain condition on right annihilators and containing no infinite direct sum of nonzero right ideals has a classical right ring of quotients that is semisimple Artinian. These two finiteness conditions define a right Goldie ring.

subject: math.RA
name: Ore theorem for domains
statement: A domain R in which aR intersects bR nontrivially for every pair of nonzero a,b admits a division ring of right fractions. R embeds in this division ring, and every element has the form ab^(-1) with a in R and nonzero b in R.

subject: math.RA
name: Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
statement: If a Lie algebra g over a field has an ordered basis (x_i), the ordered monomials x_(i_1)...x_(i_r), with i_1 at most ... at most i_r, form a basis of its universal enveloping algebra. Equivalently, the associated graded algebra is the symmetric algebra of g.

subject: math.RA
name: Maschke theorem
statement: For a finite group G and field k whose characteristic does not divide |G|, every k[G]-module is semisimple. Equivalently, every submodule has an invariant complementary submodule.

subject: math.RA
name: Hilbert basis theorem
statement: If R is a commutative Noetherian ring, then every polynomial ring in finitely many variables over R is Noetherian.

subject: math.RA
name: Chinese remainder theorem for rings
statement: For pairwise comaximal two-sided ideals I_1, ..., I_r in a ring R with identity, the canonical map from R/(I_1 intersect ... intersect I_r) to the product of R/I_j is an isomorphism.

subject: math.RA
name: Structure theorem for modules over a PID
statement: Every finitely generated module over a principal ideal domain R is isomorphic to R^r direct sum R/(d_1) direct sum ... direct sum R/(d_s), where the nonzero nonunits d_i satisfy d_1 dividing ... dividing d_s. The free rank and these invariant factors, up to units, are uniquely determined.

references.title: Structure theorem for modules over a PID

subject: math.RA
name: Rational canonical form theorem
statement: Every square matrix over a field is similar to a block diagonal matrix of companion matrices of monic polynomials f_1 dividing f_2 dividing ... dividing f_s. This list of invariant factors is unique and determines its similarity class.

subject: math.RA
name: Jordan canonical form theorem
statement: If the characteristic polynomial of a square matrix over a field splits into linear factors, the matrix is similar to a direct sum of Jordan blocks. The blocks are unique up to reordering.

subject: math.RA
name: Cayley-Hamilton theorem
statement: Every square matrix A over a commutative ring satisfies its characteristic polynomial: if p_A(t)=det(tI-A), then p_A(A)=0.

subject: math.RA
name: Krull-Schmidt theorem
statement: A module of finite length over any ring is a finite direct sum of indecomposable modules. The isomorphism classes of those summands, with multiplicity, are uniquely determined.
